title: AI Video
subtitle: Turn your brand into a short launch video with Gemini and Google Vids. Learn hooks, storyboards, camera moves, sound, editing, captions and honest AI labels.
bigIdea: A video is lots of pictures shown fast. AI video has to keep every frame matching, so short, simple, well-planned clips work best. Great videos are planned before they are made: a strong hook, a clear story, the right camera moves and good sound matter more than fancy effects.
objectives: Explain how AI makes video from frames, and why clips can glitch.
Write video prompts with the Video Prompt Formula (Subject & action · Setting · Style · Camera · Light & mood · Sound).
Plan a short ad with a hook and 4 story beats, and draw it as a storyboard.
Use camera moves, photo to video and a fixed character description to make clips that match.
Edit clips, voice, music and captions together in Google Vids, with a good pace.
Spot possible fake video, check it, and label your own AI video honestly.

vocabulary.definition: One still picture in a video. Most videos show about 24 frames every second.
vocabulary.analogy: One page of a flip book.
One Lego brick of your movie.
vocabulary.example: Gemini makes clips about 8 seconds long.

vocabulary.definition: Google's video-making AI. You use it inside Gemini and Google Vids.
vocabulary.analogy: A movie studio that fits in a chat box.
vocabulary.example: 'Make a video of a robot watering a plant.'

vocabulary.definition: The first 3 seconds of a video. It makes people stop and watch.
vocabulary.analogy: The worm on a fishing hook.
vocabulary.example: A plant gasps for water in the hot sun.

vocabulary.definition: The main parts of a story, in order.
vocabulary.analogy: The stops on a bus route.
vocabulary.example: Hook → Problem → Fix → Call to action.

vocabulary.definition: A comic-strip plan of a video, with one box for each shot.
vocabulary.analogy: A map before a road trip.
vocabulary.example: 6 boxes, each with a picture, action, camera, sound and words.

vocabulary.definition: How the camera moves during a shot.
vocabulary.analogy: Turning your head, or walking closer.
vocabulary.example: Zoom in, pan, follow, circle around, fly over.

vocabulary.definition: Giving the AI a picture and asking it to make the picture move.
vocabulary.analogy: A magic photo in a storybook that comes alive.
vocabulary.example: Upload your mascot and say 'make it wave hello'.

vocabulary.definition: A voice that talks over the video. You hear it, but don't see who's talking.
vocabulary.example: 'Meet Sip, the bottle that never leaks.'

vocabulary.definition: A short sound that makes an action feel real.
The strip in an editor that shows all your clips in order.
vocabulary.analogy: A train with a car for each clip.
vocabulary.example: Clips on top, voice and music below.

vocabulary.definition: Cutting off the slow start or end of a clip.
vocabulary.analogy: Cutting the crusts off a sandwich.
vocabulary.example: Make an 8-second clip into a 2-second shot.

vocabulary.definition: How fast a video feels. Short shots feel fast.
vocabulary.example: Most shots in a short ad last 1 to 3 seconds.

vocabulary.definition: The words of what's said, shown on the screen.
vocabulary.example: Big white words with a dark edge at the bottom.

vocabulary.definition: A fake video, picture or voice of a real person, made with AI.
vocabulary.analogy: A fake signature, but for faces and voices.
vocabulary.example: A fake video of a famous person selling a scam.

vocabulary.definition: Words or a mark that show a video was made with AI.
vocabulary.analogy: The ingredients list on a snack.
vocabulary.example: 'Made with AI' on the end card.

vocabulary.definition: The words that will be said or shown in your video, written down in order.
vocabulary.analogy: The lines actors learn before a play.
vocabulary.example: "Meet Sip Squad. The bottle that keeps up with you."

gamification.questLine: Your company loved its new look. Now it needs a launch video that people actually watch, plus a short 'how it works' explainer.
gamification.badge: 🎬 Hook Master: a finished launch ad that scores 3 or more on every rubric row.
gamification.boss: Launch Video Premiere: a 30 to 60 second ad with a hook, 4 story beats, sound, captions and an honest AI label, shown at a 'premiere'. 1-on-1: premiere for the teacher plus a guest.
sideQuests: Flip book to film: draw a 12-page flip book, film it, and compare it with a Gemini clip of the same idea (+25 XP).
Glitch Reel: collect 5 AI video glitches from your own clips, name each one, and show how you fixed it (+25 XP).
Live Foley: record 5 sound effects with objects at home and use one in your ad (+25 XP).
Deepfake news: find a real news story about a deepfake scam and explain how people could have spotted it (+25 XP).

safety.teach: Photo to video and voice tools work on real people, so this module needs clear rules: only animate your own things, objects and made-up characters. Never put a real person's face or voice into an AI video without their clear 'yes', and never make anyone 'do' or 'say' something they didn't.
Use your own voice or a preset AI voice. Never copy a real person's voice. Talk about fake voice calls used in scams.
Use music that comes with Google Vids or free music made for videos. No songs from the radio or streaming apps. No famous characters or real brands.
Every video gets a 'Made with AI' label and a note saying which parts are AI and which are yours. Ads must not show the product doing things it can't really do.
Before sharing a shocking video: stop, check the source, check for an AI mark in Gemini, and tell someone if it hurts a real person.

finalProject.title: Launch Video for Your Brand
finalProject.brief: Use the made-up company and Brand Kit from Module 1. Plan, make and edit a 30 to 60 second launch ad with Gemini (Veo) and Google Vids, plus an optional 15 to 30 second explainer. Show it at a 'premiere' and explain your choices. In a group, the premiere is for the class. 1-on-1, it's for the teacher and a guest.
deliverables: Storyboard (4 to 6 boxes) with action, camera, sound and words for each shot
Video Prompt Log with 3 or more tries for the most important shots
Final ad, 30 to 60 seconds, exported: hook, 4 beats, sound, captions, end card
AI label on the video + a 'what's AI, what's mine' note
Optional: a 15 to 30 second explainer with title cards

levels: A story, but a slow start
Strong hook and all 4 beats in order
The hook grabs everyone and every shot moves the story along
Clips follow the storyboard, with planned camera moves and a character that stays the same
Each camera move is picked for a feeling, and explained with video words
Hard to hear, or shots far too long
Sound is OK, pace is slow in places
Clear voice, fitting music, trimmed shots, good pace
Sound and cuts work together (cut on action, effects on time) and it passed the boring meter
No AI label, or untrue claims
A label, but captions are missing or hard to read
Clear AI label, true claims, captions that work on mute
Explains what's AI vs. their own work, and how they avoided tricks, copying and deepfake risks

finalProject.levelUp: Make 3 versions of the ad for 3 places: wide 16:9 for a website, tall 9:16 for phones, and a 6-second 'bumper'. That leads into the Website module!

support: Video Prompt Formula card with word lists (camera moves, moods, sounds).
A 30-second ad with 4 shots is enough. The explainer is optional.
Script starter with blanks: 'Ever ___? Meet ___. It ___. Get yours at ___!'
Group: Director and Editor roles, swapping halfway. 1-on-1: the student is the Director and you are the Editor for one scene, then swap.
If clip limits run low, use Gemini pictures with a slow zoom in Vids instead of video clips.
extension: Try a 'reveal' shot: start close on a detail, then pull back to show everything.
Make captions in a second language and check them with a speaker of that language.
Make the same ad in two moods (funny vs. calm) and test which works better with 3 people.

carryForward: The launch ad and explainer go on the brand's landing page in Module 3 (Websites & E-commerce).
